1.why: The main sans-serif text is legible with comfortable line spacing, but the monospaced Logs sections are small and densely spaced.

2.why: Instructions use short paragraphs without italics or all-caps, although the persistent Logs sections form dense blocks of text.

3.why: The interface uses a narrow responsive column with large fields and buttons, though long Logs sections require substantial mobile scrolling.

4.why: Most instructions are brief and direct, such as “Enter the six-digit code generated during setup.”

5.why: Examples are provided for the international phone number and recovery-code format, but not consistently for every input.

6.why: The long Logs blocks are not presented as required instructions, while the text needed to proceed is consistently short.

7.why: Setup secrets and recovery codes appear as plain text without visible copy buttons or download controls.

8.why: Authenticator setup explicitly requires manual entry and no QR code or equivalent alternative is shown.

9.why: The screenshots show ordinary input fields but provide no visible indication that browser autofill or password managers are supported.

10.why: Each page has a prominent step-specific heading and a large blue primary-action button.

11.why: The identity page requests three inputs and presents two action buttons, while the MFA settings page offers several separate actions at once.

12.why: Some actions produce clear confirmations such as “Setup secret generated” and “Enrolment confirmed,” but others report results only in the Logs section.

13.why: Back links and replacement-code generation provide limited recovery, but no reveal or hide controls are shown and replacement codes permanently invalidate prior codes.

14.why: No error state or error message is included in the screenshots, so its wording and corrective guidance cannot be observed.

15.why: No reading countdown is displayed, but the identity challenge is described as short-lived and authenticator codes are explicitly time-based.
